html:
A particle that reaches an alveolar macrophage is swallowed, and what happens next is decided inside the phagolysosome. The crystalline surface damages that compartment, and the damage is the signal: the same response follows from osmotic rupture with no particle present at all. Two things escape the damaged compartment, cathepsin B into the cytoplasm and, by a route the field still argues about, the cell's potassium through a channel in the plasma membrane. The potassium matters most. Its concentration inside a resting cell holds the sensor shut, and the map draws that as what it is, a brake: resting potassium inhibits the step at which NLRP3 takes up NEK7, and the efflux works by consuming the brake rather than by pushing. Cathepsin B helps the next step along, and the map keeps the uncertainty with it, since blocking the protease lowers the response substantially without abolishing it, and deleting any single cathepsin changes little.

None of this does anything in a cell that has not been primed. The sensor is scarce in a resting macrophage, and so is the interleukin-1beta precursor, and both are made only when NF-kB has been in the nucleus. The map draws that arm separately, gene by gene, because a protein level and an assembly step are different statements and a single arrow labelled "NLRP3 up" cannot carry either of them. What the two arms produce together is a platform: the sensor with NEK7, then ASC, then the protease precursor, which cuts itself and lets the active enzyme go.

The enzyme does three things, and the map draws each as a separate cut. It turns the interleukin-1beta precursor into the mature cytokine, it does the same for the interleukin-18 precursor, which the cell keeps ready without priming, and it cuts gasdermin D in two. That third cut is the one that opens the door. The C-terminal piece had been holding the protein inactive, and the N-terminal piece, once free, inserts into the plasma membrane and oligomerises into a pore. Both cytokines leave through it, and they leave from cells that are still alive: the pore is not only the instrument of a dying cell. Where the two cytokines then act, and what the particle burden does to a whole lung, is for the layers above this one.
